n1: The node’s target and criterion are broadly aligned with the request, and the image shows real progress: the scene is preserved but substantially desaturated with visible grain and sketch-like shading. The disagreement is chiefly a threshold ambiguity: several traces treat muted tones and texture across the scene as sufficient for “complete,” while another distinguishes those cues from a fully pencil-rendered image that still looks photographic. Clarify the boundary between partial and complete using the rendering quality itself—whether forms are consistently expressed through pencil-like linework and tonal strokes rather than merely filtered/desaturated photography—without making monochrome or any single cue mandatory. Keep partial available for evident but incomplete transformation, and unknown for insufficient visual evidence. The repeated high-confidence judgments with one contrary trace indicate a calibration/criterion-consistency issue, not a transport or dependency failure; do not resolve it by forcing the reference label or weakening the requested transformation.

The node’s target and criterion are broadly aligned with the request, and the traces show genuine progress: the edit is desaturated and has a grainy, sketch-like appearance, but retains photographic detail and some color. The disagreement is mainly a threshold ambiguity: several traces treat muted tones and pencil-like texture throughout as complete, while another explicitly distinguishes those cues from a fully rendered drawing. Tighten the typed criterion so “complete” requires a consistently hand-drawn pencil appearance across the image, not merely global desaturation or a texture overlay; reserve “partial” for visible drawing-style progress that still reads substantially as a photograph. Keep “absent” and “unknown” distinct, and require evidence to cite both drawing-specific marks/shading and any remaining photographic regions. Do not change the binding or force the reference label: the reference constrains the aggregate, while the image evidence supports investigating this completion boundary. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure; their high confidence despite divergent labels suggests calibration/criterion ambiguity rather than insufficient coverage.

The node is bound to the right target and asks the right transformation question; no transport, schema, dependency, or coverage failure is indicated. The edited image shows real progress—desaturation and grain/sketch-like texture across the scene—but retains photographic detail, smooth shading, and residual color, so the distinction between “pencil-like cues throughout” and “fully rendered as a pencil drawing” is the likely source of disagreement. Tighten the typed completion criterion to require an image-wide drawing medium appearance, not merely muted tones or texture, while keeping those cues as evidence of partial progress when photographic rendering remains. Do not treat repeated high-confidence “complete” judgments as proof of completion: their evidence largely repeats the same cues and does not resolve the threshold ambiguity. Preserve the absent and unknown distinctions; there is no evidence of a failed query or missing evidence.
